claims.text: The unresolved stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr originates from nanoscale chemically ordered clusters formed during thermal processing.
Nanoscale chemically ordered clusters produce local variations in elastic moduli.
Nanoscale chemically ordered clusters produce local variations in thermal expansion coefficients.
Local variations in elastic modulus and thermal expansion create heterogeneous internal thermal stresses.
The heterogeneous clustered microstructure mediates creep, microhardness, and temperature-dependent elastic responses.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is single phase and has a nominally homogeneous atomic distribution.
Thermal aging at 600–800 °C promotes nanoscale chemical ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
The clusters formed by aging have elastic properties different from those of the surrounding matrix.
The clusters formed by aging have thermal expansion properties different from those of the surrounding matrix.
Cluster-induced internal thermal stresses affect dislocation mobility and recovery mechanisms.
Relative to the as-cast condition, the aged alloy will have higher microhardness after deformation.
Relative to the as-cast condition, the aged alloy will show more pronounced temperature-dependent variations in elastic modulus.
Relative to the as-cast condition, the aged alloy will show more pronounced variations in thermal expansion.
Relative to the as-cast condition, the aged alloy will exhibit a modified creep response at 1250 °C, potentially including slower creep or altered strain-rate sensitivity.
Earlier studies indicate that cold work, aging, or creep conditions cause local microstructural changes that affect the alloy's properties.
